_meta: An attention head using ALiBi (Attention with Linear Biases), which encodes position not with an embedding added to the tokens but with a penalty added to the attention scores that grows linearly with the distance between the query and the key, used to show two properties: the bias makes attention prefer recent tokens, and because it depends only on the query-key distance it is defined at any sequence length, so the model runs on inputs longer than it was trained on -- where a learned absolute position embedding has no vector at all. In standard attention a query scores every key by a dot product; ALiBi subtracts slope*(query_pos - key_pos) from each score before the softmax, so a key one step back loses a little, a key many steps back loses a lot, and (with raw scores equal) the softmax concentrates on the nearest keys. The penalty is a fixed linear function of distance with a per-head slope; nothing is learned per position and nothing is added to the token vectors. That is why ALiBi extrapolates: the bias for a distance of 500 is just slope*500, a perfectly ordinary number, whether or not the model ever saw a sequence that long -- while a model with learned absolute position embeddings has a lookup table with one row per trained position and simply has no row for position 500. slope is the head's ALiBi slope; train_len is the length the model was trained on; query_pos is a query position within the trained range and far_query_pos is one far beyond it. The ALiBi biases, the recency-weighted attention, the translation-invariance of the bias, and the absolute-embedding table's lack of a far position are computed. Stdlib only.
